hero.title: 3(21) Fiduciary Services
hero.subtitle: Independent investment guidance while you retain decision-making authority.

blocks.text: Not every retirement plan committee wants to delegate investment authority completely. Many plan sponsors want experienced fiduciary guidance while maintaining control over the final decisions that affect their plan.

PointOak Retirement Advisors provides 3(21) fiduciary services for employers seeking independent investment recommendations, committee support, and documented fiduciary guidance. As your 3(21) investment fiduciary, we help your organization make informed decisions while strengthening the governance process behind each recommendation.

body.text: Unlike a 3(38) arrangement, a 3(21) fiduciary allows your committee to retain final authority over investment decisions while benefiting from independent recommendations and ongoing fiduciary expertise.

ERISA requires plan fiduciaries to act prudently and maintain an appropriate record of their process. A structured review process supported by an experienced 3(21) investment fiduciary can strengthen that process and help document prudent oversight.

PointOak operates as a fee-only advisor with no investment-product commissions or proprietary investment lineup. Our recommendations are made within our fiduciary role, with the interests of plan participants and beneficiaries at the center of the analysis.

Investment oversight doesn't stop after fund selection. We provide quarterly reviews, watch lists, performance monitoring, and recommendations designed to keep your investment lineup aligned with your Investment Policy Statement.
Retirement plan committees benefit from experienced guidance during meetings, investment reviews, benchmarking discussions, and governance decisions throughout the year.

blocks.text: A 3(21) investment fiduciary provides investment advice and recommendations under ERISA. We provide documented recommendations regarding investment selection, monitoring, and replacement decisions, while your committee retains final approval authority.
This collaborative approach allows plan sponsors to benefit from institutional investment expertise without giving up control over the retirement plan.

PointOak integrates investment monitoring, provider benchmarking, committee governance, and fiduciary documentation into a repeatable process that supports both regulatory coordination and better participant outcomes.
A 3(21) fiduciary relationship is often the right fit when your organization wants expert guidance while maintaining oversight of the retirement plan.

a.text: A 3(21) investment fiduciary provides investment advice and recommendations under ERISA while the plan sponsor or committee retains final decision-making authority.

items.q: What's the difference between a 3(21) investment fiduciary and a 3(38) investment manager?

a.text: A 3(21) investment fiduciary recommends investments, while the committee makes the final decisions. A 3(38) investment manager has discretionary authority within the delegated scope to select, monitor, and replace plan investments.

items.q: Does hiring a 3(21) fiduciary eliminate our fiduciary responsibility?

a.text: No. A 3(21) relationship shares fiduciary responsibility. Your committee continues making investment decisions and retains responsibility for those decisions.

items.q: How often should our investment committee meet?

a.text: Most retirement plan committees meet quarterly to review investments, fees, fiduciary documentation, and plan performance. Additional meetings may be appropriate during provider changes or major plan updates.

items.q: What services are included in a 3(21) engagement?

a.text: Typical services include investment monitoring, fund recommendations, benchmarking, committee support, fiduciary documentation, governance guidance, and ongoing ERISA consulting.
